### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — WO2 defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | No journal-specific AI policy page for Philosophy & Public Affairs was found (its Wiley 'For Authors' page at onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/10884963/homepage/forauthors.html returned HTTP 402 on every fetch attempt, and no cross-source quoted P&PA-specific AI language). What is confirmed is Wiley's publisher-wide 2025 AI guidelines, which apply to Wiley journals absent a stricter journal override: generative AI may assist with language/grammar polishing, structural clarity, idea development, literature search, and code assistance; authors must disclose AI use transparently (in Methods/Acknowledgements) and remain fully accountable for content; AI tools cannot be listed as authors. This is a publisher default, NOT confirmed as P&PA-specific, hence low signal quality and leniency is an inference, not a measured fact. |
| **Source URL** | https://newsroom.wiley.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/Wiley-Releases-AI-Guidelines-for-Authors/default.aspx |

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** Philosophical discussion of substantive legal, social, and political problems, plus more abstract questions arising from them, and studies of the moral/intellectual history of such problems when relevant to contemporary philosophical debate. Since the October 2024 editorial transition (new Editor-in-Chief Jason Brennan, Georgetown), the journal explicitly states it wants 'bold, daring, and risk-taking' papers on public concerns, and has committed to viewpoint/ideological diversity, stating 'no preference will be given to papers that affirm editors' political or moral commitments.'

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Analytic normative/political philosophy argumentation, Applied ethics on legal/social/political problems, Moral and intellectual history bearing on contemporary philosophical significance, Interdisciplinary contributions from legal scholars, political scientists, economists, sociologists engaging philosophically with public issues, Shorter 'public philosophy' pieces for lay audiences (new category since 2023/2024 transition)

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **ai_policy (journal-specific)**: The Wiley-hosted P&PA 'For Authors' page (onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/10884963/homepage/forauthors.html) returned HTTP 402 Payment Required on every fetch attempt and no search snippet quoted journal-specific AI language; only Wiley's publisher-wide 2025 AI guidelines could be confirmed, not confirmed as applied verbatim to this journal.
- **preprint.allowed**: No public source (Wiley journal page inaccessible, no forum/blog discussion found) states P&PA's preprint-posting policy explicitly; left null rather than assuming standard Wiley green-OA defaults.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No first-hand SciRev reviews (0 on file), no muchong/zhihu results, no Reddit r/AskAcademia threads found discussing reviewer tone/culture at this journal specifically. Left null rather than inventing a generic 'rigorous but slow philosophy reviewers' narrative.
- **positioning.accepts_now (recent article titles)**: Could not access the Wiley 'List of Issues' page (also behind the same 402 wall) to pull concrete 2024-2026 article titles; positioning is inferred from aims/scope statements and editorial-transition announcements rather than a sampled title list.
